What Is a Half Adder? Definition, Circuit and Expressions

A half adder is a combinational logic circuit that adds two single bits, A and B, and gives two outputs: Sum (S) and Carry (C). It is called "half" because it has no carry input, so it can only handle the least significant bit of a binary addition.

The half adder circuit diagram needs just two gates: one XOR gate for the Sum and one AND gate for the Carry.

  • Sum: S = A ⊕ B
  • Carry: C = A · B

Full Adder Carry Expression

A full adder adds A, B and a carry in (Cin). Its outputs are:

  • Sum: S = A ⊕ B ⊕ Cin
  • Carry out: Cout = A·B + Cin·(A ⊕ B), which simplifies to the majority function Cout = A·B + B·Cin + A·Cin

In the half adder and full adder circuit diagram comparison, the full adder is simply two half adders plus one OR gate: the first half adder adds A and B, the second adds that sum to Cin, and the OR gate combines the two carry outputs into Cout.
